episode_title: Would you tell your boss you want their job? | Martin Fuhrer | Siemens Healthineers Diagnostics

real_qa.q: What does Siemens Healthineers Specialty Lab Solutions business do and how are its tests used clinically?
real_qa.r: Specialty Lab Solutions at Siemens Healthineers produces products used to test blood and urine samples in clinical laboratories. These tests are used to diagnose blood diseases, blood clotting disorders, allergies, and therapeutic drug levels, as well as detect illegal drugs. Ultimately, these tests help doctors make decisions about patient diagnosis and therapy.
real_qa.requete: Siemens Healthineers Specialty Lab Solutions tests

real_qa.q: How did Martin Führer transition from clinical laboratory work to joining the medical device industry in 1991?
real_qa.r: Führer worked in a university hospital clinical lab after his studies and was impressed by visiting company representatives—service engineers, application specialists, and salespeople—who possessed deeper technical knowledge and awareness of emerging science. He wanted to become one of these industry professionals, so he joined as an application specialist and salesman in 1991.
real_qa.requete: Martin Führer 1991 industry career clinical lab

real_qa.q: What advice does Martin Führer give about communicating career aspirations to managers without risking job security?
real_qa.r: Führer told his boss directly 'I want your job' as a compliment showing the role he aspired to, and his manager responded positively with guidance on what skills and experience he needed. He emphasizes that you must communicate your interests and aspirations regularly to leadership and managers, not just during formal performance reviews, so they understand where to position you when opportunities arise.
real_qa.requete: telling boss you want their job career advancement

real_qa.q: What is reverse mentoring and how does Martin Führer implement it at Siemens Healthineers?
real_qa.r: Reverse mentoring pairs a more seasoned executive with an early-career, younger talent in the organization. Führer started this experiment about two years ago with his head of HR. The reverse mentor should not report directly to the executive, confidentiality must be protected, and in-person meetings are critical for building genuine connection and trust before honest feedback can be shared.
real_qa.requete: reverse mentoring senior executive junior talent

real_qa.q: What did Martin Führer's reverse mentor teach him about town halls and organizational communications?
real_qa.r: Führer's reverse mentor told him bluntly 'we don't care' about his carefully prepared quarterly town halls, explaining that younger employees receive information through many channels and find highly scripted, overly formal content inauthentic. This taught Führer that unscripted, human storytelling and authentic connection matter more than polished presentations to engage different generations.
real_qa.requete: reverse mentoring feedback town halls authenticity communication

guest.titre: Executive Vice President and Head of Specialty Lab Solutions
guest.bio_context: Martin Führer joined the clinical lab industry in 1991 as an application specialist and salesman, inspired by watching a bioscientist work through a microscope during childhood hospital visits. Over three decades, he remained with specialty lab diagnostics products through multiple company acquisitions, building a global career that included roles in the United States, Singapore, United Kingdom, Austria, and Switzerland. He leads approximately 1,500 people worldwide in the Specialty Lab Solutions business at Siemens Healthineers, focusing on blood and urine diagnostic tests for clotting disorders, allergies, and drug testing.
